title: A Controlled Benchmark of Deep Segmentation Architectures for Mammographic Microcalcification Segmentation on CBIS-DDSM: Evidence Consistent with an Annotation-Related Performance Limit
content: Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed cancer in women worldwide, and clustered microcalcifications on mammography are among its earliest indicators. Automated segmentation of microcalcifications is challenging because the calcifications are small, sparse, and often embedded in dense fibroglandular tissue. In addition, publicly available datasets such as CBIS-DDSM provide annotations at the calcification-cluster level rather than for individual calcification particles. Although numerous deep-learning architectures have been proposed for this task, their relative performance under a common experimental framework remains unclear. This study presents a rigorous, leakage-controlled benchmark of ten segmentation architectures, including convolutional models (U-Net, nnU-Net, BreastNet, ConvNeXt-UNet), an attention-gated model (Attention U-Net), convolution-transformer hybrids (TransUNet, Swin-UNet, MedFormer, UNETR), and MAFT-Net, a multi-scale attention network incorporating dilated convolutions, squeeze-and-excitation gating, self-attention, and gated feature fusion. All models were trained from scratch using identical preprocessing, augmentation, optimisation, and patient-disjoint train/test partitions on the CBIS-DDSM calcification subset. Performance was evaluated using Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), Intersection-over-Union (IoU), 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and classification AUC. Across all architectures, Dice scores were confined to a narrow range (0.076-0.114), with most pairwise differences failing to reach statistical significance. Increasing architectural complexity, including transformer-based models containing up to 89 million parameters, did not produce consistent performance gains. ROI occupancy analysis showed a strong positive association between Dice and annotation size, with mean Dice increasing from 0.023 to 0.255 across occupancy quartiles. These findings suggest that segmentation performance on CBIS-DDSM is influenced more by the region-level annotation format than by architectural innovation, highlighting an important limitation when interpreting reported overlap metrics.
